headline_tag: uptrend intact, but price is pausing below its 50-day line

action.title: SCALE UP acquisition budget
action.detail: The model's budget posture is to scale up acquisition: the long-run uptrend is solid, so this is a phase where spending to win new and returning users has historically paid back best, especially among active traders rather than stablecoin-only users. Because price is pausing just below its 50-day average and the Fed meets on 27-28 October, the sensible way to apply it is in steps, adding spend gradually and reviewing weekly rather than all at once. This is a budget-timing guide for the business, not trading advice.

reasons: BTC is about 11% above its 200-day average, which is still rising.
Price is up about 27% over 90 days; 76% of those days closed above the long-term average.
Price sits just below the 50-day average ($81,842), so the shorter picture is pausing.
Still about 35% below the all-time high: an early recovery, not a late-stage run.
watch: The long-run trend is up, but price has slipped just under its 50-day average and many people are still betting on a rise with borrowed money, which is what turned Friday's dip into about $846M of forced closings. A close back above $81,842 would ease that tension; a slide toward $75,547 would start a drop signal.
analysis: Bottom line: the bigger trend still points up, but this week Bitcoin is pausing just under a line that matters. Short term, the mood is calm and leans slightly up: the Fear & Greed reading is a middle-of-the-road 54, yet about $846M of bets across crypto were forced to close on Friday, mostly bets on a rise (CoinGlass via PANews), as Bitcoin briefly dipped below $80,000. If price closes above $81,842 (the 50-day average) the short term turns clearly up, below $72,955 (the 200-day average) it turns down, and in between expect choppy days. A calmer week with fewer forced sell-offs would firm this up; for now a steady, explain-the-news tone fits better than hype.

Over the next month, the picture leans moderately up. Price is about 27% higher than three months ago and about three in four of the last 90 days finished above the long-term average, but it now sits just under the 50-day average. Price first needs to win back $81,842 (the 50-day average); above $86,603 (the 90-day high) there is room to climb. The Fed's 27-28 October meeting is the next scheduled event (Reuters via PANews): reclaiming the 50-day line after it would keep growth campaigns well timed, while staying below would argue for adding new spend more slowly.

Over three to six months, the trend leans up with the most confidence of the three. Price is about 11% above its 200-day average, which is still rising slowly, and about 35% below its record, so this reads as an early recovery rather than a late-stage run. The recovery stays intact while price holds above $72,955 (the 200-day average), with $66,859 (the 200-week average) as the next floor and $124,753 (the all-time high) as the far marker. A faster-rising 200-day average would strengthen this read and support steady spending on new users; a close back under it would weaken it.
